title: A Jövő Idő: fog, tervez, majd

sections.title: Bringing Unit 27 together
sections.content: Present tense + a future time word (Jövő héten meglátogatjuk Ildikót) states a fixed, already-arranged fact. fog + a bare infinitive, conjugated for every person (fogok, fogsz, fog, fogunk, fogtok, fognak), states a prediction, intention or promise. tervez + a bare infinitive names an active plan you're deciding. majd points at the future loosely, without saying exactly when, and pairs with either present tense or fog. To negate the future, nem parks in front of fog: Nem fogok dolgozni.

sections.title: Same event, three angles
rows: Jövő héten meglátogatjuk Ildikót és Gábort.
a prediction about how it will go

items.english: What are you planning to do tonight?

items.spanish: Majd segítek neked, most nincs időm.
items.english: I'll help you later, I don't have time right now.

sections.content: Ask yourself: is this already fixed (present tense), a guess or promise about what will happen (fog), or a decision I'm actively making (tervez)? All three can appear in the very same conversation about the very same event.
